gen-dafont-good-times-gf-ovo: Good Times plants wide, geometric capitals up front with an open e and small letters as thick as bundled cable, while Ovo follows. Its thins stay close to its thicks, so paragraphs read gently.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-domine: A narrow slit where the c almost closes gives Groovy its funky, friendly grin, with loosely tracked lowercase and arms of constant width. Domine starts from the opposite instinct, with a breathing space inside every curve and a dignified classic serif feel.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-esteban: Groovy brings pipe-like strokes, loose spacing and a friendly, funky mood to the top of the pair, with a c that nearly shuts. Esteban answers with swelling, tapering curves and an oversized lowercase, so smaller text sizes should suit it fine.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-faustina: Restrained swells in the curves and an open-jawed c give Faustina a classic, authoritative voice, with capitals only slightly above the lowercase. Groovy sits over it with no thick-thin flicker at all, so a page moves from funky to steady.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-halant: Halant is traditional and authoritative, with a towering x-height, outward-pointing terminals and contrast you only notice up close. Halant gives Groovy, with its bent-tubing letters and nearly closed c, a big, short headline to play in.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-headland-one: Friendly and funky, Groovy runs its n arches as thick as the stems beside them, with a narrow slit where the c almost closes. Headland One feels dignified and open beside it.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hedvig-letters-seri: Friendly Groovy draws every line with no pressure variation, and its c almost closes into a slit. Hedvig Letters Serif opens its curves wide, with sturdy lowercase and moderate shading that feels authoritative and classic.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa reads as classic and editorial, with counters spilling into the space around them and tall lowercase that makes words look sturdy. Groovy is the loud, closed-up one; Lisu Bosa is the open one.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-marcellus-sc: Groovy is friendly and funky, with a nearly closed c, loose spacing and arms and legs of constant width. Marcellus SC is the dignified, literary half, with gentle stroke modulation and terminals pulled well back.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-montagu-slab: Groovy goes friendly and funky, its c almost shut. Montagu Slab brings robust downstrokes, slender turns, a sizable x-height and an open e channel, so reading on a screen feels traditional and refined.
